art.subject: Japanese Sparrowhawk (Accipiter gularis), adult male, as seen in Korean forests in late spring: crown, nape, back, upperwings and tail dark slate-grey; face grey; throat white with a thin, faint dark central (mesial) stripe; breast and flanks washed pale rufous-orange with faint fine barring; belly and undertail coverts white. Tail grey with several narrow dark bands. Underwing whitish with dark barring on the flight feathers. Iris deep red; cere yellow; bill short, dark and sharply hooked; legs long and thin, yellow, with long slender toes.
art.pose: perched on a branch inside dense forest, side view
art.scene: dense Korean forest interior in late spring; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Very small hawk, smaller than a Feral Pigeon and lightly built, about the length of a Brown-eared Bulbul but stockier; the smallest Accipiter in Korea. Rounded head; short, rounded wings whose tips fall well short of the tail tip at rest. Tail medium-long and square-ended, with narrow dark bands. Legs long and very thin for the size. Moves through dense forest and darts out after small birds; flight is quick flaps and short glides.
avoid: Do not paint a plain whitish underwing with black tips and a swollen orange cere (Chinese Sparrowhawk).
Do not paint a bold white supercilium or orange cheeks (Eurasian Sparrowhawk).
Do not give the adult male a yellow iris; that marks the female.
Do not paint a large, heavy hawk; this is a tiny, delicate Accipiter.
